items.title: vacuum: let the sweep release volumes that stay empty and quiet
items.body: ## Summary Fixes #11429 — the automatic vacuum sweep reclaims bytes but not slots: fully emptied volumes stay registered to their collection forever, and because `AvailableSpaceFor` counts slots only, a store at ~99% free disk can refuse every write to other collections. - New `vacuumDeleteEmptyAfterSeconds` flag (`master.` prefix under `weed server`/`weed mini`; default 0 = off). When set, the automatic sweep deletes replica copies that have stayed empty and quiet for that long — the same rule `volume.deleteEmpty` applies on demand. - The pass runs inside `Vacuum` before compaction, so an emptied volume is released rather than compacted into a still-registered empty file. Per-copy semantics mirror the shell command: remote-backed copies skipped, `onlyEmpty`/`onlyGarbage` guards carried on the wire so a copy written since the last heartbeat report is refused rather than removed. - Only a volume whose every copy is deleted leaves the sweep's work map; partial deletes just free slots on the servers that dropped their copies. Heartbeat deltas unregister the deleted copies, freeing slots for other collections. No volume-server changes needed — the `only_empty`/`only_garbage` `VolumeDelete` guards already exist in both the Go and Rust servers (#11437). #### Test plan - `TestIsEmptyVolumeDeleteCandidate`: every gate of the candidate rule (remote, read-only, live files, unreported/recent mtime, all-garbage). - `TestDeleteEmptyVolumesDeletesOnlyQuietEmptyCopies`: fake gRPC volume server — quiet-empty and all-garbage copies get `VolumeDelete` (onlyEmpty always set, onlyGarbage only for the garbage case), recent and live copies untouched, fully-deleted vids leave the map. - `TestDeleteEmptyVolumesKeepsVidWithSurvivingReplica`: a vid with a surviving replica stays in the sweep. - `go test ./weed/topology/` green; `go vet` clean on touched packages. Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai) --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a configurable vacuum setting to automatically delete volume copies that remain empty for a specified period. The setting defaults to `0`, which disables automatic deletion. * Copies are eligible when they have no remote-storage name, contain no live files, and have remained unchanged beyond the configured period. Read-only copies are eligible only when read-only deletion is allowed. * Automatic cleanup skips a volume if any replica is ineligible or cannot be reached, and keeps it in the cleanup sweep if a deletion fails. Explicit-volume vacuum requests do not run this cleanup.

items.title: shell: keep volume.tier.compact replicas on the same remote object
items.body: ## Summary - `volume.tier.compact` only processed one replica of a tiered volume: it deleted the shared remote object while sibling replicas' `.vif`/`.idx` still pointed at it, and never re-pointed them at the compacted object — leaving sibling replicas out of sync. - The download's unmount/mount also reloaded the working replica into a writable local volume mid-cycle while siblings stayed read-only. - Now the command freezes every replica (persisted, so the remount can't flip the source writable), keeps the shared object while any sibling still references it, replicates the new `.idx`/`.vif` to every replica, and lets the last tiered replica retire the old object only once it is the sole remaining holder. #### Test plan - [x] `go test ./weed/shell/` (new coverage for replica collection and the resync ordering) - [ ] Manual: compact a replicated remote-tier volume and verify all replicas converge on the new remote object Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai) --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Tiered volume compaction now coordinates updates across tiered and local replicas and synchronizes replica metadata after uploads. * Compaction failures trigger an attempt to restore uncompacted data; failures after downloading begins leave replicas read-only so compaction can be retried. * Replicas are resynchronized in an order that preserves shared remote data. * Remote deletion failures now stop local cleanup and preserve volume data, allowing deletion to be retried.

items.title: helm: render the mysql secret and env only for the mysql filer store
items.body:
Fixes #10869.

`templates/shared/secret-seaweedfs-db.yaml` and the filer's `WEED_MYSQL_USERNAME` / `WEED_MYSQL_PASSWORD` env were gated on `filer.enabled` alone. A filer on mongodb, redis, postgres or the default leveldb2 therefore got:

- a generated mysql credential secret it never reads, and `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` means it stays in the namespace forever,
- `WEED_MYSQL_HOSTNAME=mysql-db-host` and the rest of the mysql block as dead env pointing at a host that does not exist.

## Change

`seaweedfs.filer.mysqlEnabled` resolves the selected store from the merged global + filer `extraEnvironmentVars`, the same merge the statefulset already renders env from, and everything mysql-specific hangs off it: the secret, the two credential env vars, and the `WEED_MYSQL_*` keys in the filer's env, plain and secret-backed alike.

Precedence follows the merge, so a filer value overrides a global one exactly as the rendered env does. An enable flag the chart cannot read - a `valueFrom` dict, or a key in `secretExtraEnvironmentVars` - counts as selected rather than off, so a filer that really is on mysql never loses its config. `WEED_MYSQL2_*` is a separate store and is untouched, and no other store's env is touched at all.

No values were removed: with `WEED_MYSQL_ENABLED: "true"` the render is byte-identical to before.

## Rendered

default install (leveldb2):
```
env: [... WEED_LEVELDB2_ENABLED]
no test-seaweedfs-db-secret
```

`--set-string filer.extraEnvironmentVars.WEED_MYSQL_ENABLED=true`:
```
env: [WEED_MYSQL_USERNAME, WEED_MYSQL_PASSWORD, WEED_LEVELDB2_ENABLED,
      WEED_MYSQL_CONNECTION_MAX_IDLE, ... WEED_MYSQL_HOSTNAME, WEED_MYSQL_PORT]
Secret test-seaweedfs-db-secret
```

## Upgrades

The secret is a `pre-install` hook with `resource-policy: keep`, so it was never part of the release manifest and an upgrade leaves any already-created one in place. A non-mysql install that wants it gone deletes it once by hand; no new one is created.

## Tests

`helm_ci.yml` gains a block covering the issue's mongodb repro, the mysql-on render, secret-backed keys in both directions, the unreadable-flag case, and `WEED_MYSQL2_*`. The whole "Verify template rendering" step and `helm lint` against `ci/*.yaml` and `openshift-values.yaml` pass locally.

items.body: ## Summary The Go side of P1: `weed/s3api/s3vectors` serves the AWS S3 Vectors JSON API (`X-Amz-Target` dispatch), fanning data-plane calls to the shared `VectorService` gRPC (#12102). - Vector buckets map to S3 Tables table buckets; indexes map to Lance table records under a `vector` namespace plus `CreateIndex`/`DropIndex` RPCs. - Index config (dimension, distance metric, non-filterable keys) persists in the table record's `fullMetadata`. - AWS filter documents translate to Lance SQL over the `metadata` JSON column (`json_get_str`/`json_get_float`/`json_exists`); unsupported operators 400 instead of silently overmatching. - `weed s3 -port.vectors` + `-vectors.grpc` flags; both off by default, mirroring the Lance server startup. #### Test plan - [x] `go build ./weed/s3api/s3vectors/ ./weed/command/` - [ ] boto3 `s3vectors` end-to-end — conformance subset is the next PR Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai) --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added an S3 Vectors API for managing vector buckets and indexes, storing and retrieving vectors, and searching vectors with supported filters. * The API can be enabled on a separate gateway port and serves HTTP or HTTPS according to the gateway’s TLS configuration. * Added support for listing vector buckets and indexes, and for retrieving, listing, and deleting vectors. * **Bug Fixes** * The S3 gateway now stops startup when its TLS CA certificate file cannot be read or contains no valid certificates.
